title: Backups
intro: Wardarr backs up its own data: services, users, settings and history. Your media and the services themselves are not part of it.

hero.none: No backup yet. The first one runs in a few minutes, or make one now.
hero.ok: The last one is from {{last}}, the next one follows {{next}}.
hero.okNoSchedule: The last one is from {{last}}. Automatic backups are off; Wardarr still backs up before every database update.
hero.lowDisk: The last automatic backup was skipped {{when}}: the backup disk is almost full.
hero.failed: The last automatic backup failed {{when}}. Check Wardarr's log.

insight.sameDisk: Backups are on the same disk as Wardarr's data. Download important backups, or set WARDARR_BACKUP_DIR to another disk.
insight.storage: {{used}} used by backups, {{free}} free on the backup disk.

retention.title: How long backups are kept
retention.intro: One slider decides everything: how often Wardarr backs up and how the history thins out with age, like a careful person would do it.

levelHint.0: Only before database updates and restores
levelHint.2: Twice a day, about half a year back
levelHint.3: Four times a day, about a year back
levelHint.4: Every 3 hours, about two years back

retention.none: No automatic backups. Wardarr still keeps the last {{count}} backups made before a database update or a restore.
retention.keepAll_one: every backup of the last hour
retention.keepAll_other: every backup of the last {{count}} hours
retention.timelineLabel: Timeline: {{planned}} backups kept by this level over {{reach}}, {{present}} backups present now.
retention.willRemove_one: Saving removes {{count}} older backup that this level no longer keeps.
retention.willRemove_other: Saving removes {{count}} older backups that this level no longer keeps.

list.title: Stored backups
list.emptyBody: The first automatic backup runs a few minutes after the start. Backups you make or upload show up here.

restore.title: Restore this backup?
restore.body: Wardarr goes back to the state of {{date}}. Everything changed since then is replaced. Wardarr first backs up the current state, so you can go back, and then restarts. Everyone has to sign in again.
restore.older: This backup is from an older Wardarr version. Wardarr updates it after the restore.
restore.foreignKey: This backup comes from another installation. Wardarr cannot read the API keys and passwords of your services in it.
restore.acceptForeign: Restore anyway; I enter the credentials of the services again
restore.restartingBody: This takes a few seconds. The page reloads by itself.
restore.cleared_one: Enter the credentials of {{count}} service again after signing in.
restore.cleared_other: Enter the credentials of {{count}} services again after signing in.

export.title: Download with a passphrase
export.body: The file is encrypted with this passphrase and also carries the key for your stored credentials. With it, a new installation restores everything, including the API keys of your services. Without the passphrase the file cannot be opened; nobody can recover it.

delete.title: Delete this backup?
delete.body: The backup from {{date}} is deleted for good.

errors.notABackup: This file is not a Wardarr backup.
errors.backupCorrupt: This backup is damaged and cannot be used.
errors.backupTooNew: This backup is from a newer Wardarr version. Update Wardarr first.
errors.passphraseRequired: Enter the passphrase of this backup.
errors.keyMismatch: This backup comes from another installation. Confirm that you enter the credentials again.
errors.alreadyEncrypted: This backup is already protected with a passphrase.
errors.restartUnavailable: Wardarr cannot restart itself here. Restart the container to finish.
errors.backupUnavailable: Backups are not available right now. Try again in a moment.
errors.tooLarge: This file is too large for an upload.
